title: Houthis Seize Red Sea Port of Mokha, Edging Toward Bab al-Mandab, as Russia's New Jet-Powered Drones Outpace Ukraine's Air Defences
subhead: Iran-backed Houthis captured the strategic Yemeni port of Mokha in a fresh south-west offensive, bringing them within 75km of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, while Russia escalated its drone war over Ukraine with new 300mph jet-powered munitions and Kyiv lost the fortress-city front. Brazil's Supreme Court suspended sessions amid an internal corruption battle.

sections.heading: Houthis Take Mokha and Close on Bab al-Mandab
sections.body:
Yemen's Houthis have seized the strategic Red Sea port city of Mokha from Saudi-backed pro-government forces, military sources and witnesses told the BBC. Mokha's capture leaves the Iran-backed group only about 75km from Bab al-Mandab, the southern gateway to the trade route linking Asia and Europe. The Houthis said they posed no threat to international shipping but reiterated their threat to target vessels from Saudi Arabia, which has relied on the Red Sea for oil exports since the broader Iran war effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.

The offensive, launched about a week ago in Yemen's south-west, has reportedly killed hundreds and displaced thousands, with displaced families heading toward the government-held port of Aden. A Saudi-led coalition has carried out air strikes on Houthi-controlled areas in western Yemen in support of pro-government forces, while the Houthis have fired missiles and drones at cities and oil facilities in southern Saudi Arabia.
sections.whyItMatters: With Hormuz already constrained, Houthi control creeping toward Bab al-Mandab risks closing the second great energy chokepoint on Saudi shipping, compounding the pressure on global oil supply and extending the Iran-backed axis's reach over two of the world's most vital maritime routes.

sections.heading: Iran War: IRGC Strikes US Sail Drone Near Hormuz as Ships Are Hit Off Oman
sections.body:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says its navy struck a US 'Saildrone-type' unmanned vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming it 'thwarted its aggressive mission', Al Jazeera reported. Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said it received a report that projectiles hit two vessels off the coast of Oman. The exchanges mark the latest flare-up in the months-long US-Iran confrontation, which has already seen repeated US strikes on Iranian targets and Iranian missile fire on US forces and Gulf territory.

The incidents came as the IAEA's referral of Iran to the UN Security Council (first in two decades) continues to shape the diplomatic track, though no off-ramp has emerged and the military exchanges show no sign of de-escalation.
sections.whyItMatters: Attacks on US unmanned surveillance platforms and merchant vessels at the strait's entrance test how much commercial traffic the US can keep moving under escort, and signal Iran's readiness to keep probing US naval operations even as diplomacy is nominally alive.

sections.heading: Russia's Jet-Powered Drones Reshape the Air War Over Ukraine
sections.body:
Russia fired its new upgraded Geran jet-powered drones against Ukraine every day throughout August, the first time daily attacks by the faster model were recorded in Ukrainian Air Force data, BBC Verify analysis found. Ukrainian military figures put jet-powered drone attacks at 350 in June, 1,600 in July and 2,800 in August, with the new munitions outnumbering slower older models in five nightly attacks. The drones cruise at over 300mph, faster than Kyiv's interceptors, and Ukrainian intelligence says some engines are sourced from China.

The aerial escalation has coincided with fresh devastation on the ground: Ukrainian officials said a Russian drone hit a shopping mall in Pavlohrad, killing five and wounding 67 including eight children, the third strike on a mall within days after attacks in Zaporizhzhia and Sumy. Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called the mall attacks a 'tactic of coercion', and BBC reporting notes Kramatorsk and Slovyansk are now the focus of Russian ground assaults as Moscow bids to complete control of Donbas. Ukraine's air defence interception rate, once as high as 94% for long-range drones, is under pressure from the faster platform, and four Ukrainian companies are reportedly testing interceptor missiles to match its speed.
sections.whyItMatters: The shift to faster, jet-powered drones erodes Ukraine's previously strong interception record and forces Kyiv to spend scarce resources on new interceptors, at a moment when Russian ground forces are pressing the remaining population centres of Donbas — a qualitative change, not just more of the same.

sections.heading: Brazil's Supreme Court Suspends Sessions Amid Internal Corruption Battle
sections.body:
Brazil's Supreme Court cancelled a second straight day of deliberations, with Chief Justice Luiz Edson Fachin reconvening the court for Tuesday amid mutual accusations of corruption, political bias and police interference among its members, Al Jazeera reported. The crisis erupted on September 1, when Justice Andre Mendonca, a Bolsonaro appointee, unsealed federal police documents that appeared to show disgraced banker Daniel Vorcaro seeking advice from Justice Alexandre de Moraes, the judge prominent for presiding over Jair Bolsonaro's trial and ordering suspensions of platforms like X.

De Moraes has accused Mendonca of abusing his authority for political gain and requested a probe into whether Mendonca interviewed Vorcaro without police or prosecutors present. Rare cancellations at the high court underscore how institutional fault lines are colliding with Brazil's charged politics.
sections.whyItMatters: A divided Supreme Court in Latin America's largest economy erodes confidence in judicial independence just as Brazil navigates a charged election cycle, and the Mendonca-de Moraes confrontation pits a Bolsonaro appointee against the court's most powerful anti-right figure, raising the stakes for the country's democratic institutions.

sections.heading: US and German Politics: Trump's $5,000 Pledge Draws Scrutiny, AfD Debate Turns Stormy
sections.body:
President Trump's pledge to send $5,000 to every American adult — framed as a 'dividend' tied to Republican midterm wins — drew scepticism from analysts and even some of his own supporters, with the BBC reporting questions over whether the proposal is workable, legal or affordable. Al Jazeera noted observers on both sides expressed concern about the promise during the Dallas rally.

In Germany, Chancellor Friedrich Merz clashed with AfD leader Alice Weidel in a stormy debate, accusing her migration policy of amounting to 'ethnic cleansing' for skilled workers, the BBC reported, as the far-right party's recent state-level breakthrough continues to dominate the political agenda.
sections.whyItMatters: Trump's unconventional campaign promise signals how central domestic payouts are becoming to the US election debate, while Merz's sharp confrontation with the AfD shows Germany's mainstream still lacks a settled answer to the far right's momentum ahead of national contests.

bottomLine: The strategic picture tightened on two maritime and one aerial front: Houthi seizure of Mokha brings Bab al-Mandab within reach of Iran's axis, compounding an already strained energy transit map, while faster Russian jet drones are eroding the technical edge that once let Ukraine blunt Russia's long-range strikes. Brazil's Supreme Court paralysis adds a major-power institutional stress to the mix. None of the core conflicts — Iran-US, Russia-Ukraine, or the Red Sea — showed any sign of an off-ramp today; the moves were all escalatory or consolidating.
